beats.text: You are not lazy. You are not weak. You are not broken.
You are running a brain built to save energy. And once you see how it works, you can use it.
I read the research on habits so you do not have to. Here are three rules that hold up.
Rule one. Habits run on a loop. A cue, a routine, and a reward. Change the cue, and the whole loop changes.

scene.title: Find the *loop*
scene.sub: Every habit has a cue, a routine and a reward.

beats.text: Rule two. Decide in advance. Researchers call it an implementation intention. If it is seven a.m., then I put on my shoes.

scene.title: Decide *before*
scene.sub: If it is 7 am, then I put on my shoes.

scene.text: A plan made *ahead* removes the daily debate

beats.text: People who plan like this follow through far more often than people who only set a goal.
Rule three. Make it easy. Every extra step is a place to quit. Cut the friction, and starting gets lighter.
And be patient. A University College London study found it took about two months on average. Some people took far longer.
Missing one day did not ruin it. The people who kept going were the ones who came back.

scene.text: Missing once changes *nothing*. Missing twice starts a *new habit*.

beats.text: So tonight, do one thing. Write your cue, write your if-then plan, and make the first step small.
Start small, repeat it, and let the loop work for you. That is how real change is built.
